recognize_zh: 中央大型細胞含約八個彼此分開、形狀與大小一致的圓形核，細胞質豐富且帶細顆粒，這是蝕骨細胞（osteoclast）；旁邊有一個細胞質深藍、核偏心的漿細胞。
features: Very large multinucleated cell with about eight separate, uniform round-to-oval nuclei
Nuclei with fine chromatin and small nucleoli, not overlapping or lobulated
Abundant blue-purple cytoplasm with fine granules and irregular frayed borders
Nearby plasma cell with deeply basophilic cytoplasm and eccentric nucleus; scattered neutrophils
Background of smeared, grayish red cells suggesting protein-rich aspirate
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a very large multinucleated cell containing approximately eight discrete, uniform round nuclei with fine chromatin, set in abundant finely granular basophilic cytoplasm with irregular borders, consistent with an osteoclast. An adjacent cell with deeply basophilic cytoplasm and an eccentric nucleus is consistent with a plasma cell, and scattered mature neutrophils are present. The red cells in the background appear smeared and dark gray. Osteoclasts may be conspicuous in marrow aspirates from patients with active bone resorption, as in plasma cell myeloma.

ddx.vs: Megakaryocytes have a single multilobulated, interconnected nucleus rather than multiple separate uniform nuclei.
Neoplastic multinucleated plasma cells have fewer nuclei, deep blue cytoplasm with a perinuclear hof, and lack the granular pale cytoplasm of osteoclasts.
Osteoblasts are separate cells each with its own cell membrane and a pale Golgi zone away from the nucleus, rather than one syncytial cell.
Tumor clusters show nuclear pleomorphism, overlapping and molding with cell borders between cells, unlike the uniform nuclei in a single cytoplasm here.
